risks.description: Finished envelope is about 671.1 × 309.0 × 443.9 mm, larger than the listed VMC X travel and near/beyond the listed in-house saw rectangular capacity. Route assumes procured saw-cut block and indexed VMC/SPM fixturing.
risks.mitigation: Use supplier saw-cut rectangular block, build tool-room modular fixture, machine in indexed +Z/-Z/+X/-X setups with in-process datum verification.

risks.description: Several pocket, bore, spotface, and through-hole depths are not legible in the feature graph.
risks.mitigation: Use released CAD/native drawing for CAM programming; keep quotation provisional for those operations.

risks.description: Shop profile lists alkaline zinc plating in-house, but the drawing calls for cadmium plating 8-12 microns.
risks.mitigation: Use qualified outside cadmium plater or obtain customer approval for alternate coating; mask H7 bores, threads, and precision fits.

outside_processes_needed.reason: Customer hard constraint requires a solid rectangular block. Blank size exceeds listed in-house saw capacity, so procure as saw-cut block rather than forging.
Drawing requires heat treatment to 31-38 HRC; shop profile lists heat treat as outside vendor.
outside_processes_needed.sequence_position: After rough machining and pre-HT deburr; before hard finishing.

outside_processes_needed.reason: Drawing specifies cadmium plating 8-12 microns; in-house profile lists alkaline zinc plating only.
outside_processes_needed.sequence_position: After final machining, deburr, cleaning, and dimensional inspection.

outside_processes_needed.reason: Multiple positional tolerances of 0.1-0.2 mm on H7 hole patterns; in-house profile says CMM is not in house.

feasibility.assessment_notes: Feasibility is treated as confirmed by Phase 1. Manufacturing is feasible with supplier saw-cut rectangular block, custom/indexed fixtures, VMC/SPM machining, outside heat treat, outside cadmium plating, and outside CMM/FAI for the tight positional controls.

starting_dimensions.notes: Solid rectangular block per customer hard constraint. Starting dimensions use finished envelope plus approximate machining allowance: +10 mm length, +10 mm Z width/depth, +10 mm height. Confirm with CAM nesting and clamping stock.

stock.why: Customer explicitly requires rectangular-block stock and forbids forging/near-net forging. Quantity is 1000, but volume-driven forming is overridden by the hard stock-form constraint. Block allowance supports roughing, heat-treatment distortion allowance, and post-HT finishing.

evidence.cited_text: Stock form: rectangular_block — this part is machined from a solid rectangular block, NOT forged.

routing_notes: No forging or near-net forging is used; S001 is saw-cut rectangular block procurement per hard constraint.
All major rough milling precedes hole-making and heat treatment; finish milling and precision hole/bore finishing follow heat treatment.
H7 holes are drilled undersize before heat treatment and reamed after final datum finishing.
Threads are routed before heat treatment to satisfy heat-treatment sequencing; final thread gauging and masking are mandatory after HT and plating.
Cadmium plating is routed outside because shop profile lists only alkaline zinc plating in-house.
CMM/FAI is routed outside for the tight GD&T hole patterns because the shop profile states CMM is not in-house.

clarifications.question: Confirm whether cadmium plating must be performed by an approved outside cadmium plater, or whether alkaline zinc plating is an acceptable substitute.
clarifications.why_it_matters: Shop profile lists alkaline zinc plating in-house, but drawing specifies cadmium 8-12 microns.
clarifications.suggested_default: Use outside cadmium plating to drawing requirement.

clarifications.question: Provide released CAD or full drawing values for all unresolved pocket, slot, bore and through-hole depths.
clarifications.why_it_matters: Cycle formulas and CAM cannot be fully populated for several features with null depth.
clarifications.suggested_default: Keep routing provisional and program final depths from native CAD.

clarifications.question: Confirm exact heat-treatment process for 15CDV6 to achieve 31-38 HRC.
clarifications.why_it_matters: The route assumes through harden and temper, but the drawing gives hardness only, not process standard.
clarifications.suggested_default: Through harden and temper to 31-38 HRC with vendor certificate.

clarifications.question: Confirm which H7/H8 holes and bores must be plated/masked, and whether plating buildup is allowed in any internal threads.
clarifications.why_it_matters: 8-12 microns cadmium changes fit class on H7/H8 features and affects thread gauging.
clarifications.suggested_default: Mask all H7/H8 holes/bores and internal threads unless drawing specifies coating inside.

clarifications.question: Confirm if VMC indexed-fixture machining is acceptable for the 671.1 mm long housing, or whether a larger outside machining center is required.
clarifications.why_it_matters: Listed VMC X travel is 600 mm while part length is 671.1 mm.
clarifications.suggested_default: Use indexed fixtures for in-house VMC/SPM machining with in-process probing.

assumptions.text: The customer hard constraint overrides volume-driven forging selection; the stock is a solid rectangular block.
A supplier can provide the oversize saw-cut 15CDV6 rectangular block if in-house saw capacity is insufficient.
The large housing can be machined in indexed VMC/SPM fixtures despite exceeding listed VMC X travel.
H7/H8 features are masked for cadmium plating unless customer explicitly requires coating in those features.
Unknown feature depths and low-confidence extracted features will be programmed from released CAD/native drawing; routing remains provisional for those dimensions.

analysis_trace.summary: Reconstructed a very complex one-piece prismatic/3D housing in 15CDV6, approximate envelope 671.1 × 309.0 × 443.9 mm, with broad +Z/-Z faces, side bosses, datum faces, many pockets/channels/ribs, H7/H8 holes/bores, M5/M8 threads, heat treatment 31-38 HRC, and cadmium plating 8-12 microns.
issues: Many feature depths and some datum surfaces are ambiguous.
Part is larger than listed VMC X travel and likely larger than in-house saw rectangular capacity.

analysis_trace.summary: Called and used route sequences for milling, hole_making, bore_finishing, heat_treatment, and surface_treatment. Milling drives the route; hole-making and bore-finishing are embedded; heat treatment and cadmium plating are late-process interrupts.
issues: Pre-loaded milling/hole-making/bore-finishing sequences supplemented with heat-treatment and surface-treatment sequence lookups.

analysis_trace.summary: Classified as part_family=milled and base_geometry=complex. Although it contains cylindrical bosses and bores, the full component is a large prismatic housing that cannot be lathe-dominant.
issues: CNC lathe not selected due envelope and integral prismatic body.

analysis_trace.summary: Called routing corrections with milled/complex/alloy_steel and key features including pockets, precision bores, H7 holes, threads, heat treatment and coating. No corrections were returned.
Selected solid block form rather than forging due explicit customer hard constraint. Starting block dimensions use the finished envelope plus machining allowance.
issues: Block procurement likely outside because of in-house saw capacity uncertainty.

analysis_trace.summary: Built a coherent timeline: saw-cut block procurement, rough datum/pocket/profile milling, side rough bore work, pre-HT drilling/tapping, pre-HT deburr/clean, outside heat treat, post-HT finish milling, precision reaming/boring, final deburr/clean/mark, outside cadmium plating and CMM/FAI.
issues: H7 holes are final-reamed after HT to maintain tolerance; this is treated as finish sizing rather than bulk drilling.
Threads are tapped pre-HT and must be gauged after HT and protected during plating.

analysis_trace.summary: Grouped operations by access direction and machine: saw, VMC +Z, VMC -Z, VMC side, SPM drilling/tapping, finish bench, outside heat treatment, post-HT VMC, finish hole/bore setup, finish bench, and outside plating/FAI.
issues: Some formula required depths remain null because the drawing extraction did not provide them; clarification questions added.

analysis_trace.summary: Checked route order against key rules: datum faces before holes; drilling after milling; center-drill before drilling; tap last in pre-HT hole sequence; deburr before heat treatment; all coating after machining; precision features masked for plating. Feature coverage is grouped across sub-operations for all non-body features F002-F075.
issues: Final validation requires CAD and CMM program due tight positional tolerances and unresolved dimensions.
